findings.text: Each case in the routed table couples a readable label with an instruction sequence plus execution attributes and oracle data. Classic cases use the classic instruction form while internal cases use the extended internal form. Attributes select classic or internal execution and optional expected failure or no packet data behavior. Oracle data includes a sparse map from packet offsets to octet values, a list of expected outcome pairs distinguishing accepted values from zero results, and optionally an expected error code or a required stack depth.

Absolute loads read one, two or four octets from a packet offset and assemble them in network order with full unaligned support. Indirect loads add the index register to a supplied displacement before the same bounds checked read. In bounds reads return the assembled value through the accumulator. Reads that would extend past the available data take a zero result path instead of exposing out of range memory.

Cases clustered at the tail of the packet define the exact edge between acceptance and rejection for each width. A single octet at the final valid position succeeds while wider accesses starting at positions that would overrun the end fail to the zero path, including halfword and word reads that overlap the end by one or more octets.

Negative displacements derived from SKF_LL_OFF address early packet headers and behave like ordinary absolute loads with the same success or zero outcome split, including repeated successive reads. A raw negative displacement without that base is rejected during program load with EINVAL when the case is marked as an expected failure.

The multiply shift load reads the octet at its packet offset, keeps only the low nibble and scales it by four into the index register while leaving the accumulator unchanged. The derived index is observed by transferring it to the accumulator. Out of range offsets and raw negative offsets yield a zero index, while link layer based offsets yield the same scaled nibble as direct offsets.

Both accumulator and index start cleared. Addition and subtraction against the cleared peer preserve or negate as ordinary arithmetic, while multiplication by the cleared peer yields zero. Division or remainder with a zero divisor in the index register halts execution and produces a zero result rather than continuing to a later return. Division or remainder of a cleared accumulator by one also yields zero.
Equality tests against a cleared accumulator or between cleared accumulator and index take the taken branch, confirming that comparisons see initial zeros.

A set of internal jump cases checks agreement between interpreter and just in time handling of sign extension for large immediates and masked values. The cases combine moves, logical masking, wide constant loads and not equal or equal jumps with both immediate and register comparands, asserting the expected branch target for each encoding variant.

Stack loads of every width support using the same register as destination and address base. Each case stores a known pattern below R10, copies R10 into R0, then loads through R0 with a small negative displacement. A narrow stack reservation suffices, and the wide case is validated by subtracting the original pattern and folding the halves to zero.

A generated family seeds ten registers with distinct values, executes a single arithmetic operation targeting R8 or R9, normalizes that target, then verifies every register still holds its seed and returns success only if all match. Coverage spans thirty two and sixty four bit immediate and register forms of logical, shift and arithmetic operations toward two destinations, plus atomic widths in the truncated tail, requiring that any helper call implementation remain transparent to the program register file.

The table uses CLASSIC to select classic filter execution and INTERNAL to select extended internal execution. FLAG_NO_DATA marks cases that run without packet data, FLAG_EXPECTED_FAIL marks cases that must be rejected during load, and EINVAL is the expected rejection code for invalid negative absolute displacements.

Out of bounds packet reads must not access memory outside the packet and must instead follow the zero result path. Division and remainder by zero in the index register must terminate the program with zero rather than trapping or continuing. Unaligned halfword and word reads must succeed when fully in bounds.
